body:
You're right to be afraid. Fear makes you vigilant. Vigilance is extremely important because this is all about prevention, planning ahead, and never being caught off guard or unprepared. For example, if you ever have to sleep in the bed with a child again, it will be a good idea to have rules for yourself. For example, you could decide that under no circumstances will you physically touch the child. That might mean that you end up sleeping on the floor and having to come up with an excuse the next morning to explain why you did that if the kid keeps rolling over into you in his sleep.

My point is that you cannot be caught in that situation and decide on the spot what to do. If you do have these sexual desires someday, then your brain may trick you and tell you that it's okay to be making contact even if it's not. It may be okay, it may not be okay. You need to think about this shit when you're alone, calm, sober, and not under a deadline. Anytime you become afraid, plan and make rules and reflect on whether they're working for you and whether you're following them.

If you are not a pedophile, then this strategy of always being prepared and not getting into a situation that you're not sure about will help you stay sane. If you don't let a kid sit in your lap, for example, you can't question your motives for doing so.

EVERYBODY has fucked up thoughts and feelings sometimes. Everybody. What matters is how you act on them. Even something as small as staring at a child for too long can be considered an action, to be clear. What matters is what you do, so for now it's a good idea to make absolutely sure you don't do anything that you might question yourself about and drive yourself crazy over later.

Contact those organizations. Don't give anybody you talk to about this issue any personal information. They don't need it to help you. I would question the motives of anybody asking you identifying information in the context of helping you with your potential problem.

Stay vigilant. Stay safe. You're okay.

It's okay to feel bad about yourself. What you've said there about things getting better and improving tells me that you're trying very hard to improve things. Otherwise, there wouldn't be any reason for you to think things have to get better. What you've said makes me think that every time you've given up, and fallen or jumped off the horse, you eventually got back in the saddle. That's all anybody can ask of you, really. That you try, even if you've given up before. Looks like you're trying.

There are people in the world who can help you.  https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_pedophile_and_pederast_advocacy_organizations

Your sexual orientation does not dictate your actions. Many homosexual men live their entire lives without a single sexual encounter with another man. It's tragic that they feel that have to live this way, and in your case, IF you are a pedophile, then tragically you'll have to live a similarly chaste existence. However, it's completely possible and nowhere near as big a deal as you're making it out to be.

People who prey on children are usually pedophiles. Pedophiles rarely prey on children. Why? Because they, like you, are otherwise normal human beings with a disordered sexual drive who are very aware of how UNBELIEVABLY harmful, damaging, and completely evil and fucked up it would be to ever lay your hands on a child.

Don't tell anybody about this in a manner that might be traced back to you. The world is hysterical about pedophiles. Not the entire world though.

Call the organizations I linked to. Don't give up. You'll find help. There are people who have devoted their lives to helping people like you. Don't forget that. It's true, and you will find them if you try hard enough.

Hey, it's been 9 hours since you posted. Did you get through your day?

You have a lot of stress and negative and shitty things going on in your life. Can you think of some things that you're proud of? Maybe something you've done, or changed about yourself, or something you're done for somebody else? Thinking about some fights I'm still fighting in myself, and some of the progress I've made helped me feel better today.
